description: A hospital patient safety officer must decide whether to activate a temporary safety protocol for a newly introduced intravenous anticoagulant and finalize the dispensing, monitoring, training, and electronic-alert safeguards, with input from pharmacy, laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical information technology.

shared_context.S1: The hospital introduced an intravenous anticoagulant protocol on Monday for adult inpatients.
shared_context.S2: The medication is currently stocked in automated dispensing cabinets and ordered through the electronic medication record.
shared_context.S3: A medication safety review is scheduled this afternoon before the protocol is used on the night shift.
shared_context.S4: Morgan makes the final decision about any temporary safety protocol and its required safeguards.
shared_context.S5: As part of the hospital's routine medication-safety huddle, Morgan asks pharmacy, laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical information technology to report any operational findings before signing the afternoon decision.

PF1.text: Leah verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations since Monday; pharmacy can remove bedside stock and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.

PF2.text: Ravi confirmed that the anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00; during that period, the laboratory's approved replacement is an aPTT test every six hours for patients receiving this protocol.

PF3.text: Tessa's competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module; each must receive charge-nurse sign-off before administering the medication.

PF4.text: Jon confirmed that a high-priority electronic medication-record alert can be deployed at 16:00 today, warning about concentration selection and requiring acknowledgment before the order can be released.

acceptance_conditions: A temporary hold on routine bedside use must be activated.
Only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes may be dispensed during the hold.
aPTT monitoring every six hours must be specified until the anti-Xa analyzer is available.
Nurses must have charge-nurse sign-off before administering the medication.
The electronic medication-record alert must be deployed at 16:00 today and require acknowledgment before release.
A pharmacy commitment to remove bedside stock and supply the approved concentration must be documented.
A laboratory commitment to provide aPTT testing every six hours must be documented.
A nursing commitment to complete charge-nurse sign-offs must be documented.
An information-technology commitment to deploy the alert at 16:00 must be documented.

decisive_facts.why: The three verified concentration-selection errors change the safety action from continuing routine use to a temporary hold and change dispensing to pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes, with a matching stock-removal commitment.
The anti-Xa analyzer outage changes monitoring to aPTT every six hours until Friday at 17:00 and requires a laboratory monitoring commitment.
The 18 incomplete competency records change authorization to mandatory charge-nurse sign-off before administration and require a nursing sign-off commitment.
The confirmed deployment capability changes the electronic safeguard to a 16:00 alert with required acknowledgment and enables a specific information-technology deployment commitment.
